source_text:
ἑψόμεθα· πόθεν; ἀγένητον δὲ εἶναι πιστεύομεν ὡς ἐξ ἀγενήτου Πατρὸς τὸν ἐξ αὐτοῦ

13

φύντα Λόγον· κεφαλὴν δὲ ὠνομάσθαι φαμὲν παντὸς ἀνδρὸς ὡς ἀρχέτυπον μὲν, ὡς
ἔφην, ἐπειδὴ δὲ πέφηνεν ἄνθρωπος ἐν ἐσχάτοις τοῦ αἰῶνος καιροῖς, καὶ ὡς ἀνθρώποις
ὁμόφυλα κατά γε τὸ ἀνθρώπινον εἰς "κεφαλὴν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ, ἥτις ἐστὶ "τὸ σῶμα αὐτοῦ·"
πρωτεύει γὰρ αὐτὸς ἐν πᾶσι κατὰ τὴν τοῦ Παύλου φωνήν. Πᾶς ἀνὴρ προσευχόμενος ἢ
προφητεύων κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων καταισχύνει τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ κ.τ.λ.
Ὁρᾷς ὅπως τοῦ ἑκατέρῳ πρέποντος βραβευτὴν ποιεῖται 283 καὶ ὁριστὴν τὸν τῆς
φύσεως νόμον; ἀνδράσι μὲν γὰρ ἡ παῤῥησία πρεπωδεστάτη, γυναικὶ γεμὴν τὸ
ἐγκαλύπτεσθαι κόσμος· οὐκοῦν ὕβρις εἰς τὸ ἀρχέτυπον εἴη ἂν καὶ μάλα εἰκότως, τῆς
εἰκόνος τὸ ἀκαλλές· εἰ γάρ ἐστιν ἀνὴρ εἰκὼν καὶ δόξα Θεοῦ, πεποίηται γὰρ κατὰ τὰς
γραφὰς οὕτως, σωζέτω Θεῷ τὴν πρέπουσαν παῤῥησίαν, ἀκατακάλυπτον ἔχων τὴν
κεφαλὴν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπιτιμώσης αὐτῷ τῆς φύσεως εἴς γε τὸ ἐκκαλύπτεσθαι δεῖν·
ἐλεύθερον γὰρ τὸ θεῖον καὶ πέρα μώμου παντὸς, ἰδίᾳ τε δόξῃ καταπλουτοῦν καὶ
τεθαυμασμένον. καὶ εἴπερ ἐστὶν ἡ γυνὴ καθ' ὁμοίωσιν ἀνδρὸς, καὶ εἰκὼν εἰκόνος, καὶ
δόξης δόξα, νομοθετεῖ δὲ αὐτῇ καὶ τὸ κομᾶν ἡ φύσις, τί τὸ πρῶτον φιλονεικεῖ τὸ
ὑστερίζον ἐν χάριτι; κατ' εἰκόνα μὲν γὰρ καὶ αὕτη καὶ ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ, πλὴν ὡς διὰ
μέσου τοῦ ἀνδρὸς, ὥστε κατά τι παραλλάττοι βραχὺ τὴν φύσιν· οὐ γράψομαι αἰδοῖ
περιστέλλουσαν, ὡς ἔνι, τὸ ζῷον καὶ στεφανοῦσαν τῇ κόμῃ· τὸ γάρ τοι παῤῥησιάζεσθαι,
γυναιξὶν οὐκ ἀζήμιον. οὐκοῦν κατακαλυπτέσθω φησὶ διὰ τοὺς ἀγγέλους, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι
τοὺς ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις ἐνιδρυμένους παρὰ Θεοῦ. οὐχ ὅτι πάσχουσί τι ἐν τῷ ὁρᾶν
γυναῖκας· ἄνθρωποι μὲν γὰρ τὸ παχὺ δὴ τοῦτο καὶ ἀπὸ γῆς ἔχοντες σῶμα, καὶ ταῖς
ἐμφύτοις ἡδοναῖς πρὸς τὰ αἰσχίω κατωθούμενοι, πάθοιεν ἂν τὸ βλάβος, ταῖς γυναίων
ὥραις ἐφ' ἃ μὴ πρόσηκεν ἐρεθιζόμενοι· περὶ δέ γε τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων, τί ἄν τις ἔχοι
τοιοῦτον ἢ νοεῖν ἢ φράσαι; ἅγιοι γάρ εἰσι καὶ ῥύπου παντὸς ἀμείνους ὅτι καὶ ἔξω σαρκὸς
λεπτοῖς τε καὶ νοητοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὑπὲρ νοῦν τὸν ἀνθρώπινον κεχρημένοι σώμασιν· ἀλλ'
ὅτι δυσφοροῦσι λίαν εἰ ἀμελοῖτο πρός τινος ὁ τοῦ πρέποντος νόμος. πρέποι δὲ γυναιξὶ
τὸ κατακαλύπτεσθαι· καὶ τούτου μάρτυς ἡ φύσις· ἡ γὰρ κόμη φησὶν ἀντὶ περιβολαίου
δέδοται 284 αὐτῇ. τηρείσθω τοίνυν καὶ ἐπ' αὐτῷ τὸ πρέπον διὰ τοὺς εἰδότας ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς
τὴν τοῦ δημιουργήσαντος βούλησιν. Χρῆται γεμὴν ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος εὐτεχνίᾳ πάλιν
ἑτέρᾳ· ἔφη μὲν γὰρ κατ' εἰκόνα καὶ ὁμοίωσιν Θεοῦ πεποιῆσθαι τὸν ἄνδρα· κατόπιν δὲ
τῆς αὐτοῦ τιμῆς τε καὶ δόξης οἷον ἐῤῥίφθαι τὸ θῆλυ, διισχυρίσατο σαφῶς ἐπάγων τὸ
ἑξῆς Ἡ γυνὴ γάρ φησι δόξα ἀνδρός ἐστιν· οὐ γὰρ ἐκτίσθη ἀνὴρ διὰ τὴν γυναῖκα ἀλλὰ
γυνὴ διὰ τὸν ἄνδρα· εἶτα περιστέλλων εὖ μάλα ἐφ' οἷς ἦν εἰκὸς λυπεῖσθαι τὸ θῆλυ,
προσεπάγει καί φησι Πλὴν οὔτε γυνὴ χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς οὔτε ἀνὴρ χωρὶς γυναικός. γέγονε
μὲν γὰρ ὁμολογουμένως ἐξ ἀνδρὸς ἡ γυνὴ, καὶ τοῦτό ἐστιν ἀληθές· εὕρηται γεμὴν εἰς
ἀνδρὸς γένεσιν οὐκ ἀσυντελής· συνενεγκοῦσα δὲ ἄμφω πρὸς ἓν ἡ φύσις, ἀλλήλων ἐν
χρείᾳ κατεστήσατο οἰκονομικῶς συνείρουσα πρὸς ἀγάπην· Θεὸς δὲ ὅτι τῶν ὅλων ἐστὶν ὁ
δημιουργὸς, προσεμπεδοῖ λέγων Τὰ δὲ πάντα ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ, παρῆκται γὰρ εἰς τὸ εἶναι τὰ
πάντα διὰ Χριστοῦ.

ΤΟΜΟΣ Ε.
ΛΟΓΟΣ Α.
Οὐδεὶς ἐν πνεύματι Θεοῦ λαλῶν λέγει Ἀνάθεμα Ἰησοῦν κ.τ.λ. Ὁ ΚΥΡΙΟΣ ἡμῶν

14

Ἰησοῦς ὁ Χριστὸς ἐπηγγέλλετο μὲν ἀπελθὼν πέμψειν ἡμῖν τὸν παράκλητον· προσετίθει
δὲ τούτοις τό "Ἐκεῖνος ἐμὲ δοξάσει." συνίεμεν δὲ ἡμεῖς καὶ μάλα ὀρθῶς ὅτι δοξάζει
Χριστὸν τὸ Πνεῦμα αὐτοῦ, καὶ σοφοὺς ἀποτελοῦν τοὺς ἐν οἷς ἂν γένοιτο, καὶ αὐτὸν τοῖς
ἁγίοις ἐνοικίζον δι' ἑαυτοῦ· ἔστι γὰρ ἐν ἡμῖν διὰ τοῦ Ἁγίου Πνεύματος· δοξάζει δὲ καὶ
pass_a_gloss: [Completing u04-open: ‘but not their stupidities (ἀβελτερίαι)’] we will follow (ἑψόμεθα); whence? We believe the Word (Λόγος) sprung (φύντα) from him to be uncreated (ἀγένητον) as from an uncreated Father; and we say he has been named head (κεφαλή) of every man as archetype (ἀρχέτυπον), as I said, but since he appeared man in the last times of the age, and as things of same race (ὁμόφυλα) with men according to the human, into ‘head for the church, which is his body’; for he is first (πρωτεύει) in all according to Paul’s voice. [Lemma] Every man praying or prophesying having (something) down on the head shames his head, etc. You see how he makes the law of nature (τῆς φύσεως νόμος) umpire (βραβευτής) and definer (ὁριστής) of what befits each? For to men openness (παρρησία) most fitting, to woman being covered (ἐγκαλύπτεσθαι) an ornament (κόσμος); so it would be an outrage (ὕβρις) to the archetype, very reasonably, the unloveliness (ἀκαλλές) of the image (εἰκών); for if man is image and glory (δόξα) of God, for he has been made so according to the scriptures, let him keep for God the fitting openness, having the head uncovered, and nature not rebuking (ἐπιτιμώσης) him as to needing to be uncovered; for the divine is free and beyond all blame (μῶμος), enriched in own glory and wondered at. And if the woman is according to likeness (ὁμοίωσις) of man, and image of image, and glory of glory, and nature legislates (νομοθετεῖ) for her also wearing long hair (κομᾶν), why does the later (ὑστερίζον) in grace contend (φιλονεικεῖ) with the first? For she too according to image and likeness of God, except as through the middle of the man, so that in some respect she differs (παραλλάττοι) slightly in nature; I will not indict (γράψομαι) her wrapping (περιστέλλουσαν) with modesty (αἰδώς), as possible, the living being (ζῷον) and crowning with the hair; for to be open (παρρησιάζεσθαι) for women not without penalty (ἀζήμιον). So let her be covered, he says, because of the angels, clearly those settled (ἐνιδρυμένους) in the churches by God; not that they suffer something in seeing women; for humans having this thick (παχύ) and from-earth body, and pushed down (κατωθούμενοι) by innate (ἔμφυτοι) pleasures to baser things, might suffer the harm, provoked (ἐρεθιζόμενοι) by women’s bloom (ὥραι) to what is not fitting; but of the holy angels, what such thing could one think or say? For they are holy and better than all filth (ῥύπος), since also outside flesh and using thin (λεπτοῖς) and intelligible (νοητοῖς) and beyond-human-mind bodies; but because they are very vexed (δυσφοροῦσι) if the law of the fitting (τὸ πρέπον) be neglected by someone. Being covered would befit women; and witness of this nature; for the hair, he says, has been given her instead of a wrap (περιβόλαιον). Let the fitting be kept therefore also in it, because of those knowing beyond us the will (βούλησις) of the one who created. The divine Paul uses again another artfulness (εὐτεχνία); he said the man made according to image and likeness of God; and that behind his honor and glory the female is as it were thrown (ἐρρίφθαι), he insisted (διισχυρίσατο) clearly adding what follows ‘For the woman is glory of man; for man was not created because of the woman but woman because of the man’; then wrapping round (περιστέλλων) very well the things at which the female would likely be grieved, he adds and says ‘But neither woman without man nor man without woman.’ For admittedly the woman came from man, and this is true; but she is found toward man’s generation (γένεσις) not non-contributing (ἀσυντελής); nature having brought both together to one established them in need of each other, economically (οἰκονομικῶς) linking (συνείρουσα) to love (ἀγάπη); and that God is creator (δημιουργός) of all, he further fixes (προσεμπεδοῖ) saying ‘But all things from God,’ for all things were brought (παρῆκται) into being through Christ. [Heading] Tome 5. Discourse (λόγος) 1. [Lemma] No one speaking in the Spirit of God says ‘Anathema Jesus’ etc. Our Lord Jesus the Christ promised, having gone away, to send us the Paraclete (παράκλητος); he added to these ‘That one will glorify (δοξάσει) me.’ We understand very rightly that his Spirit glorifies Christ, both making wise those in whom it may come to be, and housing (ἐνοικίζον) him in the saints through itself; for he is in us through the Holy Spirit; and it glorifies also [ἑτέρως ‘otherwise’, which opens u04-rem-mid].
pass_b_english: But we shall not follow their foolishness. How could we? We believe that the Word who sprang from the Father is uncreated, as being from an uncreated Father. And we say that He has been called the head of every man (1 Corinthians 11:3), as the archetype, as I said; but since He appeared as man in the last times of the age, and as one of the same kind as men in His humanity, He was given as head to the Church, which is His body (Ephesians 1:22–23). For He holds the first place in all things, as Paul says (Colossians 1:18).
“Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head,” and so on (1 Corinthians 11:4).

Do you see how he makes the law of nature the judge and arbiter of what befits each? For openness is most fitting for men, while for a woman being veiled is an adornment. So the unseemliness of the image would quite reasonably be an insult to the archetype. For if man is the image and glory of God (1 Corinthians 11:7), as according to the Scriptures he was made (Genesis 1:27), let him keep before God the openness that befits him, with his head uncovered, since nature does not reproach him for having to go uncovered. For the Divine is free and beyond all blame, rich in its own glory and held in wonder.

And if woman is in the likeness of man, an image of an image and a glory of a glory, and nature also lays it down for her to wear long hair (1 Corinthians 11:15), why should what comes second in grace contend with what is first? For she too is according to the image and likeness of God (Genesis 1:26), but as it were through the mediation of man, so that in some small respect she differs in nature. I will not bring a charge against her when she wraps her person in modesty as far as she can and crowns it with her hair; for to go openly uncovered is not without harm for women.

So, he says, let her be veiled because of the angels (1 Corinthians 11:10), clearly meaning those whom God has stationed in the churches. Not that they suffer anything in seeing women. Human beings, who have this coarse body taken from the earth and are pushed down toward baser things by inborn pleasures, might suffer harm, being stirred by the beauty of women toward what is not fitting. But as for the holy angels, what could anyone think or say of that kind? For they are holy and above all defilement, since they are outside the flesh and have bodies that are fine and spiritual, beyond the grasp of the human mind. Rather, it is because they are deeply grieved if anyone neglects the law of what is fitting.

And being veiled befits women, and nature is witness to this: “for her hair,” he says, “has been given to her as a covering” (1 Corinthians 11:15). So let what is fitting be kept in this matter too, because of those who know the will of the Creator better than we do.

The inspired Paul uses yet another skilful device. He said that man was made according to the image and likeness of God, and he plainly insisted that the female has been cast, as it were, behind his honor and glory, adding what follows: “For woman,” he says, “is the glory of man; for man was not created for the sake of woman, but woman for the sake of man” (1 Corinthians 11:7, 9). Then, gently covering over what would likely grieve women, he goes on to say, “Nevertheless, neither is woman without man, nor man without woman” (1 Corinthians 11:11).

For woman admittedly came from man, and this is true (1 Corinthians 11:12); yet she has been found to have her share in bringing man into being. Nature, bringing both together into one, has made them need each other, wisely binding them together in love. And he further confirms that God is the Creator of all things, saying, “But all things are from God” (1 Corinthians 11:12); for all things were brought into being through Christ (John 1:3).

“No one speaking in the Spirit of God says, ‘Jesus is accursed,’” and so on (1 Corinthians 12:3). Our Lord Jesus Christ promised that when He had gone away He would send us the Comforter (John 16:7), and to this He added, “He will glorify Me” (John 16:14). And we understand, quite rightly, that His Spirit glorifies Christ both by making wise those in whom He comes to dwell and by making Christ dwell in the saints through Himself; for Christ is in us through the Holy Spirit. And He glorifies Him also in another way…

choices.why: Single nu: 'not come into being', not ἀγέννητος.
ῥίπτω is 'throw, cast'; οἷον softens it to 'as it were'.
Perceived by the mind rather than the senses; 'intelligible' would be jargon.
